name: Ramona Penn
life: “I still remember a goodbye drink poured before the final pay arrived.” On Saturday, near the entrance to the Wash House, Ramona stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
voice: I left the contractor over favoritism. They still owe me two goodbye shifts and a borrowed radio.
appearance: Ramona has short black hair swept back, a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, and a favorite piece of clothing, an unlined tan jacket. It usually goes with a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring. When somebody else has the floor, Ramona starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak.
personality: Ramona has a talent for getting adversaries to laugh at exactly the same thing. Ramona knows better than to expect the laugh to settle what they are arguing about.
agenda: To recover the goodbye shifts and the borrowed radio.
family: Eli Carr is Ramona’s second cousin. Ramona sets the time to leave. Eli picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The thirteenth doughnut*, Eli says, “My father's flour route paid for my first drum kit.”
connections: Jesse Arnett. A borrowed radio and a statement from a seafarer travel back to the break room.

reactions.situation: The contractor offers selected workers a partial payment
reactions.response: Ramona asks that the offer be written down with the remaining unpaid hours.

reactions.response: Ramona asks the cashier quietly which item can be set aside without making the customer explain their finances to the line.

reactions.situation: When people declare an argument over too soon
reactions.response: Ramona asks them to describe one concrete thing that will be different tomorrow.
